rea.scope: Static syntax reconnaissance on unchanged factory bodies wrapped as object literals. The partial call graph does not prove execution. The separate original-routine execution supplies request and action proof.

originalExecution.permission: When user_access_personalized_recs is absent, allow unless dsa-mode-enabled is 1; otherwise allow unless user_access_personalized_recs is 0. The original menu is also disabled while offline. Product Free/Premium is not overridden.
originalExecution.action: Read body.mediaItems[0].uri, run the original URI parser, and navigate to its playlist URL path. No playback call is made.
cases: different arbitrary song URIs and locales
first returned playlist selected from multiple results
originalExecution.substitutions: Node WHATWG URL/URLSearchParams; inert React elements/hooks, presentation/localization/shortcut boundaries, supplied product state and online status, synthetic credentials, and a recording transport returning synthetic playlist URIs. Exact substitutions and source ranges are in the fixture.
originalExecution.browserFields: Decoded GET/preflight headers and ordering inherit the separately captured original renderer GET in native-renderer-lyrics.json. The application URL, query, headers and options come from unchanged original song-radio, RequestBuilder and SpotifyTransportRequest execution. This is not a new radio-specific browser wire capture.

dartPort.ownership: Pass the caller's cancellation token through the session/token owners, CORS and H2/H3 transport. Cancel on replacement, navigation, sign-out or disposal. Ignore duplicate pending clicks and stale completions. No radio polling or speculative media/license work.
dartPort.playback: Open the returned ordinary playlist. Its existing Play control supplies real playlist context and music rows to the existing player. No advertising or synthetic playback reporting is introduced.
dartPort.diagnostics: Redact a Spotify URI contained in a path segment to :id. Queries, credentials, bodies, rotation and build-mode destinations remain outside this change.

verification.originalExecution: 7 original menu scenarios executed; 4 enabled cases independently produced requests and playlist destinations.

live.hotReload: succeeded on an existing isolated debug runtime
live.session: existing saved Accounts grant, retaining its selected HTTP token provider
live.songSeed: a real song already described by that runtime; identifiers and account data omitted
live.scope: The new resolver reached Spotify and the existing playlist repository opened the returned playlist. This probe did not start audio or interrupt the installed release's playback.

tests: test/song_radio_test.dart: independent original permission/request/header/preflight/response fixtures; rejected responses; real menu/navigation cancellation, duplicate-click suppression and explicit playlist Play
test/http_status_log_test.dart: actual persisted request and response records redact the radio seed URI
verification.privacyRegression: The persisted-log test fails against an isolated copy with the old redactor because it writes the raw spotify:track seed. The same test passes against the changed owner.

limits: Original proprietary routines are from the previously captured 1.3.6.1921 renderer. Live acceptance does not prove whole-client compatibility with the currently installed 1.3.9.2055 build.
No Chromium code was decompiled. TLS, QUIC, HPACK/QPACK and radio-specific browser wire parity are outside this proof.

Synthetic menu fixtures establish original offline/DSA gates; live verification establishes the available authenticated session only. The app uses its real session readiness and server denial, without inventing entitlements.

The navigation widget check disables semantics and supplies an empty playback-bar builder, following the existing shell checks. It proves menu routing and playback intent, not accessibility or audible playback.
Radio playback reuses the existing playlist and license path; this feature does not resolve the separate license-reliability backlog.
